Rashi on Eruvin 59b:10:1.hebrew: ולא שבק לה שיור - ועיר של רבים והרי היא של רבים הוה, מדקאמר ליה: "עיר של יחיד ונעשית של רבים", אלמא ההיא שעתא דרבים הוה. ואמרו ליה אינהו: מעיקרא נמי דרבים הוה, אלא אשפה הוה לה שסותם אחד [סגי לה] מפתחיה, ולא היה לה אלא פתח אחד; ואמר לעיל דאפי' של רבים בהכי הוה סגי ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:10:1.english: And did not leave any remainder for it - And [this town] was [originally] a city of the public and is [presently] of the public, from [the fact] that he said to him: "[I thought it was] a city of an individual that became of the public," which shows that at that time it was of the public. And they [the elders] said to him: Originally as well it was of the public; rather, it had a garbage dump that blocked one [— it was sufficient for it —] of its entrances, and it had only one entrance, and it was stated above that even for [a city] of the public, with this it was sufficient for it.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:13:1.english: A ladder - By which they ascend and descend [to] outside its [the city's] wall.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:14:1.hebrew: תורת מחיצה עליו - כלומר, אינו מבטל את הסתימה להיות כפתח:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:14:1.english: It has the status of a partition - That is to say, it does not nullify the closure to become like an entrance.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:14:2.hebrew: בסולם שבין ב' חצירות - ואין ביניהן פתח, וזה הסולם רחב ד' ביניהן — הרי הוא כשתי חצירות ופתח ביניהן, דאמרינן בפ' חלון (לקמן עירובין דף עו.): רצו מערבין אחד — עירוב אחד לשתיהן, וישתמשו זו בזו דרך גובה הכותל ודרך נקבים וסדקין; דאי לא הוי פתח, אין מערבין אחד, ולא מצו לאשתמושי דרך חורין וסדקין:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:14:2.english: In [the case of] a ladder between two courtyards - And there is no entrance between them, and this ladder, four [handbreadths] wide, is between them — it is [treated] like two courtyards with an entrance between them, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Ḥallon (below, Eruvin 76a): [If] they wish, they make one [eiruv] — one eiruv for both of them — and they may use [one courtyard] from the other over the height of the wall and through holes and crevices; for if it were not [considered] an entrance, they could not make one [joint eiruv], and they would not be able to use [one from the other] through holes and crevices.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:14:3.hebrew: רצו שנים מערבין - שני עירובין: אלו לעצמן, בני בתים של חצר, שלא יאסרו זה על זה להוציא מבתיהן — שהן רשות המיוחדת לכל אחד — לתוך החצר, שהוא רשות כולן; ואלו לעצמן, ולא ישתמשו זו בזו:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:14:3.english: If they wish, two establish an eiruv - [Meaning,] two eiruvin: these [residents make an eiruv] by themselves — the householders of [one] courtyard — so that they will not prohibit one another from carrying out from their houses — which are a domain designated for each individual — into the courtyard, which is the domain of all of them; and these [residents of the other courtyard make an eiruv] by themselves, and they may not make use of one [courtyard] in the other.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:15:1.hebrew: ומי אמר ר"נ הכי - דתורת מחיצה עליו לקולא:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:15:1.english: And did Rav Naḥman say this? - That it has the status of a partition for leniency.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:15:2.hebrew: מרפסת - אלדויי"ר בלע"ז. דיורי עליות סמוכות זו לזו ופתוחות לחצר, ועושין מרפסת על פני אורך עליות, ופותחין לה פתחי כולן, ועולין ויורדין דרך סולם של מרפסת לחצר, ודריסת רגליהן ויציאתן לרשות הרבים דרך החצר הויא. לפיכך, אם אינן מערבין עם הדיורין התחתונים, אוסרין אלו על אלו להוציא כלי הבתים לחצר:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:15:2.english: A balcony - aledoir in Old French. [In a case of] residents of upper stories [that are] adjacent to one another and open to the courtyard, and they construct a balcony along the length of the upper stories, and open the doorways of all of them into it, and ascend and descend by way of the ladder of the balcony to the courtyard, and their right of passage and their exit to the public domain is through the courtyard — therefore, if they do not join in an eruv with the downstairs residents, they restrict one another from carrying articles from the houses into the courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:1:1.hebrew: ואין לה אלא פתח א' - ולאו מפולשת היא, ולא דמי לדגלי מדבר:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:1:1.english: And it has only one entrance - And it is not open through, and does not resemble the banners of the wilderness.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:3:1.hebrew: אלא לאורכה - דרך עיירות להיות פתחי פילושיהן לאורכם, ורה"ר עוברת מפתח לפתח, וחלוקה לאורכה. הלכך, אין בני עבר הלז רשאין לערב לבדן ובני עבר הלז לבדן, משום דהני והני דרסי בהך רה"ר, ויוצאין ונכנסין דרך פתחים לכאן ולכאן, ורה"ר זו מחברתם שכולם מעורבין בה, ואסרי אהדדי:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:3:1.english: Only along its length - It is the way of towns for their through-and-through openings to be along their length, and a public domain passes from gate to gate, and [the city's] division is along its length. Therefore, the residents of this side are not permitted to establish an eiruv on their own and the residents of that side on their own, because both these and those tread upon this public domain and exit and enter through the gates on this side and on that side; and this public domain joins them, as they are all intermingled in it, and [consequently] they restrict one another.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:3:2.hebrew: אבל לרחבה - בני שני העברים לראש האחד לבד, ובני שני העברים לראש השני לבד — מערבין; שהרי יכולין להסתלק אלו מאלו, ולא יהא דרך לאלו על אלו, ובוררין להן: אלו פתח שאצלן, ואלו פתח שאצלן:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:3:2.english: But across its width - The residents of both sides [of the street] at the one end alone, and the residents of both sides at the other end alone, may establish an eiruv; for they are able to separate from one another, so that these do not have passage through those, and they select for themselves: these, the entrance adjacent to them, and those, the entrance adjacent to them.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:4:1.hebrew: פלוגתא דרבנן ור"ע בפרק הדר (לקמן עירובין דף עה.):
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:4:1.english: [The] dispute of the Rabbis and Rabbi Akiva [is] in the chapter [entitled] Hadar (below, Eruvin 75a).

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:4:2.hebrew: רגל המותרת במקומה אוסרת שלא במקומה - כגון ב' חצירות זו לפנים מזו, והחיצונה פתוחה לרה"ר, והפנימית אין לה פתח לרה"ר אלא יוצאת דרך חיצונה. ולא מיבעיא היכא דעירבו דיורין שבחיצונה לבדן, ובני פנימית לא עירבו ביניהן לבדן להיות מותרין בתשמיש חצר לעצמו, דהויא רגל אסורה במקומה, דאסרה דריסת הרגל דידהו אחיצונה אפי' לרבנן — דכיון דבחצר דגופייהו אסרי, ליכא למכפינהו למיחד דשא דידהו וימחלו על דריסת הרגל שיש להן על החיצונה — אלא אפי' עירבו זו לעצמה וזו לעצמה, דהויא פנימית מותרת במקומה, פליג ר"ע ואומר: דריסת הרגל דידה אסרה אחיצונה, ופנימית מותרת וחיצונה אסורה; והכי נמי ניתסרו אהדדי:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:4:2.english: A foot that is permitted in its own place prohibits [in a place] not its own - For example, two courtyards, one inside the other, where the outer [courtyard] opens to the public domain and the inner [courtyard] has no entrance to the public domain, but rather exits through the outer [courtyard]. And it is not only [the case] where the residents in the outer [courtyard] established an eiruv on their own, and the residents of the inner [courtyard] did not establish an eiruv among themselves on their own to be permitted in the use of the courtyard for itself — such that it is “a foot that is prohibited in its own place,” which prohibits [carrying in] the outer [courtyard] through their right of passage even according to the Rabbis, for since they are prohibited in their own courtyard, one cannot compel them to lock their door and waive the right of passage that they have over the outer [courtyard] — rather, even [if] this [courtyard] established an eiruv for itself and that [courtyard] for itself, such that the inner [courtyard] is permitted in its own place, Rabbi Akiva disagrees and says: Its right of passage prohibits [carrying in] the outer [courtyard], so the inner [courtyard] is permitted and the outer [courtyard] is prohibited. And so too here, [the two halves of the city] should prohibit one another.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:7:1.hebrew: דפנימית אחדא דשא ומשתמשא - דכיון דמותרת במקומה, כגון זו כופין על מדת סדום, שלא יהא לה היום דריסת הרגל על החיצונה, אלא תסגור דלת שביניהן ותשמש במקומה:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:7:1.english: As the inner [courtyard] closes the door and uses [its own] - For since it is permitted in its [own] place, [in] a case such as this we coerce [against] the conduct of Sodom, so that it will not have right of passage today over the outer [courtyard]; rather, it must close the door between them and use its [own] place.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:7:2.hebrew: אבל הכא - הרי רשות הרבים של אלו ושל אלו אחד הוא, שאין בו חילוק באמצע אורכו ולא רמז של מחיצה לומר: תיחוד דשא ותשמש את כולה במקומה. והיכי מצית לסלק הני מהני:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:7:2.english: But here - Behold, the public domain of these [residents] and of those [residents] is one, as there is no division in the middle of its length nor [even] a hint of a partition to say, 'Let it close [a] door and use all of it in its [own] place.' And how can you remove these from those?

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:8:1.hebrew: מבוי נמי אסרי אהדדי - דכיון דמעיקרא של יחיד הוה, והיו מערבין את כולה והורגלו להיות אחד — אסרי אהדדי. ואפי' איכא לחי או קורה למבוי, לא מהני:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:8:1.english: [Each] alleyway as well, they should prohibit one another - For since originally it was [a town] of an individual, and they would make an eiruv for all of it and became accustomed to being [as] one, they prohibit one another; and even if there is a sidepost or crossbeam for the alleyway, it is of no avail.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:9:1.hebrew: דעבוד דקה - פתח נמוך בראש כל מבוי, דגלו אדעתייהו לאסתלוקי כל חד מחבריה:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:9:1.english: Where they made a dakah - A low doorway at the entrance of each alleyway, for they revealed their intention to withdraw, each one from the other.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:9:2.english: For his entrance - For the entrance of his courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 59b:9:3.hebrew: אינו אוסר על המבוי - אם לא נשתתף עמהן, דגלי אדעתיה דאסתלק:
Rashi on Eruvin 59b:9:3.english: Does not prohibit [the residents of] the alleyway - If he did not participate with them [in the shituf], for he has revealed his intention that he has withdrawn [from it].

Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:10:1.hebrew: ולא שבק לה שיור - משמע דאי שבק לה שיור הוה עביד שפיר, ולא הוה פריך ליה אביי מידי. וא"כ משמע כפי הקונט' דפי' במתני' דשל רבים והרי היא של רבים מהני ליה שיור. וכן משמע לקמן (עירובין דף ס.) גבי מחוזא דמהני ליה שיור, אע"ג דהיא של רבים, כדמשמע בפ"ק (דף ו:); ומעיקרא נמי היתה של רבים, דאי של יחיד, לא היתה צריכה שיור. והא דנקט במתני' "של רבים ונעשית של יחיד", לאשמועונ' דאע"ג דנעשית של יחיד, בעיא שיור:
Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:10:1.english: “And did not leave a remainder for it” - This implies that had he left a remainder for it, he would have acted properly, and Abaye would not have raised any objection to him. And if so, this implies in accordance with the Kuntres [Rashi], who explained on the Mishnah that for [a city that was] of the public and is [still] of the public, leaving a remainder is effective for it. And so it is also implied below (Eruvin 60a) regarding Mechoza, that leaving a remainder is effective for it even though it is of the public, as is implied in the first chapter (6b); and originally too it was of the public, for if it had [originally] been of an individual, it would not have required a remainder. And as for that which [the Mishnah] stated, “of the public and became of an individual,” [it was] to teach us that even though it became of an individual, it requires a remainder.

Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:13:1.hebrew: בעא מיניה כו' מרבה - לא גרס "מרבה בר אבוה", דעליו לא היה אומר רב נחמן "לא תציתו ליה", דרבו היה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:13:1.english: "He raised a dilemma, etc., before Rabba" - The text does not read "from Rabba bar Avuha," as regarding him Rav Nachman would not have said, "Do not listen to him," since he was his teacher.

Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:14:1.hebrew: תורת פתח עליו בסול' שבין ב' חצירות - תורת מחיצה עליו להקל — היה יכול למצוא נמי בסולם שבין ב' חצירות, כגון שרצפו בסולמות:
Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:14:1.english: "It has the status of an entrance in [the case of] a ladder between two courtyards" - [An application where] "it has the status of a partition upon it" to be lenient, [the Gemara] could also have found in [the case of] a ladder between two courtyards, such as where one lined [the breach] with ladders.

Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:4:1.hebrew: כמאן דלא כר"ע - וא"ת: ולרבנן, לארכה נמי יערבו לחצאין, שיערבו מצד א' כל מבוי ומבוי בפני עצמו, וליתיב כולה רה"ר לצד השני, דהשתא בני כל מבוי ומבוי מותרין כל אחד וא' במקומו, ולא יאסרו שלא במקומן (*):(*)? וי"ל: דלא דמי; דשני חצירות זו לפנים מזו, רגל הפנימי המותרת במקומה אינה אוסרת שלא במקומה על החיצונה, דאחדא לדשא ומשתמשא, ומסתלקא מלהשתמש בחיצונה, דעיקר תשמיש דחצר החיצונה לבני חיצונה היה, והויא פנימית בחיצונה שלא במקומה. אבל הכא, אף ע"ג דכל מבוי ומבוי מותר כל אחד ואחד במקומו, מודו רבנן דאסרי רה"ר על צד האחד, דהא מקומן הוא, דרה"ר הוי להני כמו להני. ולרחבה דמערבין, מדמי השתא לב' חצירות, משום דיש לאלו רה"ר ופתח וכן לאלו, ואין צריכין להשתמש בני פתח זה בצד פתח האחר. ובדאיכא דאמרי קאמר: אפי' לרחבה אין מערבין, דלא מצי להסתלק מר"ה כלל, אע"ג דאית להו רה"ר כנגדו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:4:1.english: In accordance with whose [opinion]? It is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva - And if you say: But according to the Rabbis, they should also be able to establish an eiruv for halves along its length: namely, that on one side each and every alleyway should establish an eiruv on its own, and let all of the public domain be assigned to the second side; for now, the residents of each and every alleyway would be permitted, each one in its [own] place, and they would not prohibit [the other side] in a place that is not their own (*):(*)? And one can say: It is not comparable. For [in the case of] two courtyards, one inside the other, the foot of the inner [courtyard], which is permitted in its own place, does not prohibit [the residents of] the outer [courtyard] in a place that is not its own, because [the resident of the inner courtyard] closes the door and uses [her own courtyard], and withdraws from using the outer [courtyard], for the primary use of the outer courtyard belonged to the residents of the outer [courtyard], and the inner [courtyard] in the outer [courtyard] is [in an area that is] not its place. But here, even though each and every alleyway is permitted, each one in its [own] place, the Rabbis concede that they prohibit the public domain to the [other] side, because it is their [own] place, as the public domain belongs to these just as [it belongs] to those. And [the case of dividing the city] along its width, where they may establish an eiruv, [the Gemara] now compares to two courtyards, because these have a public domain and an entrance, and so do those, and the residents of this entrance do not need to use the side of the other entrance. And according to [the version of] "there are those who say," it states: Even along its width they may not establish an eiruv, because they are unable to withdraw from the public domain at all, even though they have a public domain opposite it.

Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:7:1.hebrew: דפנימית אחדא דשא ומשתמשא - ומה שפי' בקונט', "שלא יהא לה דריסת הרגל על החיצונה" — לאו דוקא, דליכא קפידא בדריסת הרגל; דא"כ, היתה מסתלקת לגמרי מרה"ר, דהא דרך חיצונה נפקא, ואין לנו לסלקה מרה"ר, כדאמרי' הכא: "מי מצי מסלקי להו רה"ר מהכא?". אלא "תיחוד דשא" — מלהשתמש בחיצונה קאמר; וכן עשיית דקה דשמעתין — לענין תשמיש, לא לענין הילוך:
Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:7:1.english: "As the inner [courtyard] closes the door and uses [its own]" - And that which was explained in the Kuntres, "that it should not have right of passage through the outer [courtyard]," is not exact, for there is no objection to right of passage. For if so, it would be cut off entirely from the public domain, since it exits by way of the outer [courtyard], and we have no [basis] to cut it off from the public domain, as we say here: "Can they remove the public domain from here?!" Rather, "[it] should close the door" means [in order to refrain] from using the outer [courtyard]; and similarly, the making of a dakkah [partition] in our sugya is regarding use, not regarding passage.

Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:7:2.hebrew: אבל הכא מי מצי מסלקי כו' - פי': דוקא פנימית אחדא דשא מלהשתמש בחיצונה שאינה מקומה, דעיקר חיצונה לבני חיצונה; אבל רה"ר הוי להני כמו להני. ובחנם פ"ה דברה"ר אין חילוק באמצע ארכו, ולא רמז מחיצה, לומר "תיחוד דשא ותשמש":
Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:7:2.english: "But here, are they able to remove, etc." - Explanation: Specifically the inner [courtyard] closes the door [to refrain] from using the outer [courtyard], which is not its place, as the outer [courtyard] fundamentally belongs to the residents of the outer [courtyard]; but the public domain belongs to these [residents] just as [it does] to those. And unnecessarily did Rashi explain that in the public domain there is no division in the middle of its length, nor a hint of a partition, to say "let it close the door and use [its area]".

Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:8:1.hebrew: מבוי מבוי נמי אסרי אהדדי - פי' בקונט': כיון דמעיקרא של יחיד הואי, והיו מערבין את כולה, והורגלו להיות אחד — אסרי אהדדי; ואפי' איכא לחי או קורה למבוי, לא מהני. וקשה לר"י, דאמר בפ"ק (דף יד:): "עושה לחי לחצי מבוי — יש לו חצי מבוי", אלמא משתרי חצי מבוי בפני עצמו, אע"פ שהורגלו לערב כל המבוי יחד! ומיהו איכא לאוקמא לההיא בדליכא חצירות פתוחות למבוי מן הלחי ולהלן:
Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:8:1.english: For each alleyway, they should also prohibit each other - [Rashi] explained in the commentary: Since originally it belonged to a single individual, and they would make an eiruv for all of it, and they became accustomed to being one [domain], they prohibit each other; and even if there is a side-post or a crossbeam for the alleyway, it is not effective. But this is difficult to the Ri [Rabbeinu Yitzchak], as it says in the first chapter (daf 14b): "If one places a side-post at the halfway mark of an alleyway, he has [permitted use of] half of the alleyway" — which shows that half of an alleyway can be permitted on its own, even though they had been accustomed to making an eiruv for the entire alleyway together! However, that [teaching] can be established [as referring to a case] where there are no courtyards opening into the alleyway from the side-post and further on.

Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:9:1.hebrew: דעבוד דקה - מחיצה גבוה ד' (ס"א י') טפחים, כגון איצטבא בפני המבוי. ובקונט' פירש: "פתח נמוך בראש כל מבוי". וכפירושו נראה, מדאמר בריש כל גגות (לקמן עירובין דף פט:): "בנה עלייה ע"ג ביתו ועשה לפניה דקה, הותר בכל הגגין כולן", ולא יתכן לפרש שם אלא לשון פתח. ומיהו, בסוף פירקין פ"ה: דקה — מחיצה:
Tosafot on Eruvin 59b:9:1.english: Where they made a dakkah - A partition four (other texts [read]: ten) handbreadths high, such as a bench in front of the alleyway. And in the Kuntres [Rashi] explained: "A low entrance at the head of each alleyway." And his explanation appears [correct], since [the Gemara] says at the beginning of Kol Gagot (below, Eruvin 89b): "If one built an upper story on top of his house and made a dakkah in front of it, he is permitted [to carry] on all the roofs," and it is not possible to interpret [the term] there other than as meaning an entrance. However, at the end of our chapter the Kuntres explained: dakkah [means] a partition.
